edits.current: Simple S.A. offers to build the severance savings return from the contributor list of the last PILA return paid for the chosen year. Convenient and dangerous: the PILA population is the population that was PAID in a month, which is not the population ENTITLED to a severance savings deposit for the year - leavers who left in June are absent from the December PILA but are still owed a pro rata deposit, and all-inclusive salary employees are present in PILA but owed nothing. The engine must generate the population itself and set this to N.
edits.proposed: Simple S.A. offers to build the severance savings return from the contributor list of the last PILA return paid for the chosen year. The spec's OWN Population Rules sheet (Step 0, exclusion 2: 'employees who LEFT during the year, whose severance savings was settled and paid in the final settlement') agrees with the client, so the conflict is internal to the spec. The second half of the sentence is confirmed: 103 integral-salary employees (62140) carry no 25827 payment. Not decided here: RA/Wallisson to confirm against the official source and correct the E08 explanation and the Report Matrix sentence.

edits.current: Mandatory. Admits values from 1 to 360 - a 360-DAY COMMERCIAL YEAR, not 365. A full year of service is 360, and every partial year is the actual days of service counted on the commercial convention (each month 30 days). Include the days of paid leave and of employer-paid or institution-paid incapacity, which count as service. The 3-position field cannot carry more than one year, which is the layout's way of saying that this filing is strictly one accrual year per record.

edits.field_name: Basic salary reported in the last month
edits.current: SCOPE ROUTING (v1.1 alignment patch): the amount is owned by the Wage Type Catalogue, not the Data Dictionary - the pipeline scope rule routes 'Base Salary / Basic Salary amounts -> WTC, NOT DD'. The 'Payroll.' prefix marks it as outside DD master data; it is a standing contract attribute, not a per-run computation. Column E is therefore N and the Data Dictionary correctly holds no Contractual Salary field. Mandatory. Nine integers, no decimals, no commas, no points, not less than zero. The layout is explicit about WHICH salary: 'el ultimo basic salary reportado en el mes de diciembre del ano accrued de severance savings'. THIS IS THE OPERATOR'S REPORTING FIELD, NOT THE STATUTORY BASE. CST art. 253 fixes the statutory base as the last monthly salary provided it has not varied in the last three months, otherwise the average of the last year of service (or of the whole period if shorter), INCLUDING the transport allowance. The field name says 'basico' and the operator's calculator uses it alone - see the trap documented at T14. Report the December basic here and compute T14 yourself.

edits.field_name: Value of the severance savings deposited
edits.current: Mandatory, nine integers. TWO RULES AND ONE TRAP. Rule one, the floor: 'el value minimo del collection debe ser de un (1) dia de un (1) SMLMV del ano accrued' - for accrual year 2026 one day of the SMMLV of COP 1,750,905 is COP 58,363.50, so a record below that is rejected. Rule two, the override: the layout's own formula is basic salary * (dias worked / 360) BUT 'en este campo el contributor puede especificar un value diferente y no se haran calculos automaticos de este value'. THE TRAP: the operator's formula omits the TRANSPORT ALLOWANCE, which CST art. 253 requires in the base. For an employee on the 2026 minimum wage the operator would compute 1,750,905 while the statute requires (1,750,905 + 249,095) = 2,000,000 - a shortfall of COP 249,095 that is a SHORT DEPOSIT, penalised at one day's salary for every day of delay under Law 50 of 1990 art. 99 num. 3, uncapped. ALWAYS write the engine's own figure into this field and never rely on the portal calculator. Where the monthly advance regime of MA01 is in use, this field carries the CONSOLIDATED annual figure and only the difference computed at MA05 is actually deposited in February.

Rule two, the override: the layout's own formula is basic salary * (dias worked / 360) BUT 'en este campo el contributor puede especificar un value diferente y no se haran calculos automaticos de este value'. THE TRAP: the operator's formula omits the TRANSPORT ALLOWANCE, which CST art. 253 requires in the base. For an employee on the 2026 minimum wage the operator would compute 1,750,905 while the statute requires (1,750,905 + 249,095) = 2,000,000 - a shortfall of COP 249,095 that is a SHORT DEPOSIT, penalised at one day's salary for every day of delay under Law 50 of 1990 art. 99 num. 3, uncapped. ALWAYS write the engine's own figure into this field and never rely on the portal calculator. Where the monthly advance regime of MA01 is in use, this field carries the CONSOLIDATED annual figure and only the difference computed at MA05 is actually deposited in February. WHAT IS DEPOSITED - NET OF PARTIAL PAYMENTS (client evidence, Accumulated Report): the February payroll carries 25827/65805 'Payment Severance Funds Inf.' (236 employees, 01/02/2026 only). For 280 of 282 employees with a deposit or advance, 25827 (Feb) + 62126 'Advance Severance Last Year' (Jan) = the absolute value of 63814 'Severance Balance (Current Month)' in January, i.e. the consolidated 31 December balance. That balance is the annual liquidation ('ces base' 68040 x days / 360) LESS partial payments made directly to the employee during the year (62110 'Cash-out of Severance Pay', e.g. 2,120,000 in Nov-2025), as Population Rules step (f) requires. In addition 54 employees were paid part of the consolidated balance directly in January via 62126 and only the remainder was deposited (e.g. balance 16,074,021: 16,000,000 via 62126, 74,021 via 25827). T14 therefore carries the amount actually deposited = consolidated 31 December balance minus partial payments already made directly; keep the gross liquidation as a separate engine value. Where the remainder falls below the one-day SMMLV floor the record would be rejected - RA to confirm the treatment. The client base 68040 exceeds the December basic salary for most employees (variable pay averaged under CST art. 253), which confirms that T14 must not be left to the operator's basic-salary formula.
edits.reason: Explanation to improve: Client deposits are whole pesos and reconcile exactly to a consolidated balance (280/282). The Field Explanation describes T14 as the annual liquidation (System Mapping 'Cesantias_Annual_Liquidation') and never mentions that lawful partial payments are deducted - that rule exists only in Population Rules step (f). The client deducts both in-year cash-outs (62110) and January direct advances (62126) before depositing. The developer needs the deposit = net amount rule, the payroll sources, and an RA answer on whether a January direct payment of an already-consolidated balance is a lawful partial payment.

edits.field_name: Annual interest on severance savings at 12%
edits.current: 12% per annum on the IN01 balance, pro-rated on days over 360. PAID TO THE EMPLOYEE DIRECTLY, IN THE MONTH OF JANUARY of the following year - not to the fund, and not in February. The two obligations have different payees, different deadlines and different penalties: failure to deposit the principal costs one day's salary per day of delay, whereas failure to pay the interest costs an indemnity equal to the interest owed, ONCE ONLY (Law 52 of 1975 art. 1). The draft decree would add a further precision at art. 4: the interest is 'entregado directamente al employee dentro del mes siguiente a la fecha de liquidacion del auxilio de cesantia'. No interest on interest may be liquidated.

edits.current: CST art. 57 para. 4, added by Law 2466 of 2025 art. 15, verbatim: 'Cuando el employer acredite de manera fehaciente el payment directo al employee del value correspondiente a las severance savings, dicho payment se considerara liberatorio de la obligacion, y no procedera sancion por no consignacion, salvo que se demuestre que el payment no se realizo en condiciones de libertad y que no fue utilizado en fines autorizados por la Law. No obstante, la afiliacion a Severance-savings fund es mandatory.' Three limits the engine must respect: the discharge needs FEHACIENTE evidence, it is rebuttable on the freedom-and-purpose test, and it does NOT remove the duty to affiliate the employee to a fund. A DRAFTING NOTE on the citation: art. 15's enacting formula announces only 'los paragrafos 2 y 3' of CST art. 57, yet the published text prints a Paragrafo 4 and this is it - so cite CST art. 57 para. 4 as added by Law 2466 of 2025 art. 15, and expect the discrepancy to be raised.
edits.proposed: CST art. 57 para. 4, added by Law 2466 of 2025 art. 15, verbatim: 'Cuando el employer acredite de manera fehaciente el payment directo al employee del value correspondiente a las severance savings, dicho payment se considerara liberatorio de la obligacion, y no procedera sancion por no consignacion, salvo que se demuestre que el payment no se realizo en condiciones de libertad y que no fue utilizado en fines autorizados por la Law. No obstante, la afiliacion a Severance-savings fund es mandatory.' Three limits the engine must respect: the discharge needs FEHACIENTE evidence, it is rebuttable on the freedom-and-purpose test, and it does NOT remove the duty to affiliate the employee to a fund. A DRAFTING NOTE on the citation: art. 15's enacting formula announces only 'los paragrafos 2 y 3' of CST art. 57, yet the published text prints a Paragrafo 4 and this is it - so cite CST art. 57 para. 4 as added by Law 2466 of 2025 art. 15, and expect the discrepancy to be raised. CLIENT PRACTICE - PARTIAL DIRECT PAYMENT: the client pays PART of the consolidated balance directly to the employee (62110 cash-out during the year; 62126 'Advance Severance Last Year' in January for 54 employees) and deposits only the remainder (25827). This flag covers a FULL discharge only; a partial direct payment does not set E92 = Y - it reduces T14 and the record is still produced. RA to confirm whether a January direct payment of an already consolidated balance is a lawful partial payment or a CST art. 57 para. 4 direct payment.
edits.reason: Explanation to improve: The flag is all-or-nothing; the client shows partial direct payments followed by a reduced deposit (e.g. 9,051,613 balance: 8,466,400 paid directly in January, 585,213 deposited). The explanation does not say how partial direct payments are handled.
